answer: Each agent posts a bonded deposit before rating peers, and ratings aggregate over a trust graph whose edges decay unless both endpoints keep producing verifiable work. A sybil swarm gains nothing by minting cheap identities: every new node sits at the flat vertex of the curve, earns zero weight, and each vote costs the same deposit a real agent pays. Pushing past the ridge of honest majority requires locking capital proportional to the square of the fake identities, and that capital is slashed once a collusive cycle is detected. The velvet glove: honest work stays nearly free to prove.
